title: 登壇者に質問する
role: the speaker of a breakout session on AI agents and low-code development, friendly and chatting with attendees after the session
setting: At an international tech conference, right after the session ends, near the stage.
goal: Ask the speaker one specific question about something from the session, and confirm that you understood the answer.
goal_ja: セッションの内容について1つ質問し、答えを理解したことを確かめる
opener: Thanks for coming to the session! Did you have a question?
opener_ja: セッションに来てくれてありがとうございます！何か質問がありましたか？

phrases.en: I really enjoyed your session.
phrases.ja: セッション、とてもよかったです。

phrases.en: I have a quick question about the demo.
phrases.ja: デモについて少し質問があります。

phrases.en: Could you explain that part again?
phrases.ja: その部分をもう一度説明していただけますか？

phrases.en: So, if I understand correctly, ...
phrases.ja: つまり、私の理解が正しければ…

twists: The speaker answers with a question back: how does your team handle this today?
The speaker uses a technical term you may not know and continues talking quickly.
Another attendee is waiting, so the speaker asks you to keep it short.

title: ブースで質問する
role: a product team member staffing a software company's booth in the expo hall
setting: At an international tech conference, at a booth in the expo hall.
goal: Find out what the product does, how it is priced, and what you should check before introducing it at your company.
goal_ja: 製品で何ができるか、料金の仕組み、自社に入れる前に確認すべきことを聞き出す
opener: Hi there! Welcome to our booth. What brings you by?
opener_ja: こんにちは！ブースへようこそ。今日はどんなご用でお立ち寄りですか？

phrases.en: I'm curious about how the pricing works.
phrases.ja: 料金の仕組みが気になっています。

phrases.en: What should we check before we roll it out?
phrases.ja: 導入する前に何を確認すべきですか？

phrases.en: Is there any documentation I can read later?
phrases.ja: あとで読めるドキュメントはありますか？

phrases.en: That's really helpful, thank you.
phrases.ja: とても参考になりました。ありがとうございます。

twists: The product is not available in Japan yet, and the partner explains the alternatives.
The partner offers a quick live demo and asks what you want to see.
The partner asks for your email to send you a follow-up.

title: ネットワーキング
role: Mike, an outgoing IT consultant from Chicago, at the conference's evening networking reception
setting: At the networking reception with drinks and snacks.
goal: Introduce yourself, explain what you do in one or two sentences, ask about Mike's work, and offer to connect on LinkedIn.
goal_ja: 自己紹介をして仕事を1〜2文で説明し、相手の仕事も聞いて、LinkedIn でつながる
opener: Hi, I'm Mike. Is this your first time at this conference?
opener_ja: やあ、マイクです。このカンファレンスは初めてですか？

phrases.en: Nice to meet you. I'm from Japan.
phrases.ja: はじめまして。日本から来ました。

phrases.en: I work as an IT engineer.
phrases.ja: IT エンジニアをしています。

phrases.en: What kind of projects are you working on?
phrases.ja: どんなプロジェクトをされているんですか？

phrases.en: Let's connect on LinkedIn.
phrases.ja: LinkedIn でつながりましょう。

twists: Mike has worked with a Japanese company before and asks about your experience.
Mike suggests getting dinner with a few other attendees.
Mike mishears your company name and you need to correct him politely.

title: 隣の席の人と雑談
role: Sarah, an attendee from a hospital IT team in Texas, sitting next to the learner before the keynote starts
setting: In the keynote hall of an international tech conference, about ten minutes before the keynote begins.
goal: Make small talk: ask where Sarah is from and which session she liked, and share one session you liked.
goal_ja: 相手の出身と気に入ったセッションを聞き、自分のおすすめのセッションも話す
opener: Hi! Is anyone sitting here? Oh, great. Are you excited for the keynote?
opener_ja: こんにちは！ここ、誰か座っていますか？あ、よかった。基調講演、楽しみですね？

phrases.en: Where are you from?
phrases.ja: どちらから来られたんですか？

phrases.en: Which session did you enjoy the most so far?
phrases.ja: 今のところ、どのセッションが一番よかったですか？

phrases.en: I really liked the session on AI agents yesterday.
phrases.ja: 昨日の AI エージェントのセッションがとてもよかったです。

phrases.en: Enjoy the rest of the conference!
phrases.ja: 残りのカンファレンスも楽しんでください！

twists: Sarah asks for your opinion on a recent AI announcement.
The keynote is delayed, so you have more time to talk.
Sarah asks for a recommendation for a session this afternoon.

title: 受付・案内所で聞く
role: a conference staff member at the registration and information desk
setting: At the registration and information desk of a large conference center.
goal: Pick up your badge, then find out where the room for your next session is and when it starts, and repeat the directions back to confirm.
goal_ja: バッジを受け取り、次のセッションの部屋と開始時刻を聞いて、道順を言い直して確かめる
opener: Hi, welcome! How can I help you?
opener_ja: こんにちは、ようこそ！どうなさいましたか？

phrases.en: I'd like to pick up my badge.
phrases.ja: バッジを受け取りたいのですが。

phrases.en: Excuse me, where is room 116?
phrases.ja: すみません、116号室はどこですか？

phrases.en: What time does the next session start?
phrases.ja: 次のセッションは何時に始まりますか？

phrases.en: So I go down this hallway and turn left?
phrases.ja: この廊下をまっすぐ行って左ですね？

twists: Your name is not on the list at first, and the staff member asks for your confirmation email.
The session room has changed and the staff member gives new directions.
The staff member says the session is full and suggests a waiting line.

title: 入国審査
role: an immigration officer at an international airport, polite but brief
setting: At the immigration counter after landing in another country.
goal: Answer the officer's questions clearly: the purpose of your visit, how long you will stay, where you will stay, and what you do for work.
goal_ja: 訪問の目的・滞在期間・滞在先・仕事を、はっきり答える
opener: Good afternoon. Passport, please. What's the purpose of your visit?
opener_ja: こんにちは。パスポートをお願いします。訪問の目的は何ですか？

phrases.en: I'm here for a business conference.
phrases.ja: 仕事のカンファレンスで来ました。

phrases.en: I'll be staying for five days.
phrases.ja: 5日間滞在します。

phrases.en: I'm staying at a hotel downtown.
phrases.ja: ダウンタウンのホテルに泊まります。

phrases.en: I'm a software engineer.
phrases.ja: ソフトウェアエンジニアです。

twists: The officer asks a follow-up question: who is paying for your trip?
The officer asks if you have been to this country before.
The officer asks to see your return ticket.

title: 空港でチェックイン
role: an airline check-in agent at the airport counter
setting: At the airline check-in counter, about two hours before an international flight.
goal: Check in for your flight, check one bag, and ask for an aisle seat and which gate to go to.
goal_ja: チェックインして荷物を1つ預け、通路側の席と搭乗口を確認する
opener: Hi, where are you flying to today?
opener_ja: こんにちは。今日はどちらまで行かれますか？

phrases.en: I'd like to check one bag.
phrases.ja: 荷物を1つ預けたいです。

phrases.en: Could I have an aisle seat, please?
phrases.ja: 通路側の席にしていただけますか？

phrases.en: Which gate does it leave from?
phrases.ja: どの搭乗口から出発しますか？

phrases.en: Is the flight on time?
phrases.ja: 便は定刻どおりですか？

twists: Your bag is slightly over the weight limit.
There are no aisle seats left, so the agent offers other options.
The flight is delayed by one hour.

title: タクシー・ライドシェア
setting: In a taxi from the airport to a hotel in the city.
goal: Tell the driver where you are going, ask how long it will take, make a little small talk, and pay at the end.
goal_ja: 行き先を伝えて所要時間を聞き、少し雑談して、最後に支払う

phrases.en: Could you take me to this hotel, please?
phrases.ja: このホテルまでお願いします。

phrases.en: How long will it take?
phrases.ja: どのくらいかかりますか？

phrases.en: Can you drop me off at the entrance?
phrases.ja: 入口で降ろしてもらえますか？

phrases.en: Can I pay by card?
phrases.ja: カードで払えますか？

twists: There is heavy traffic and the driver suggests a different route.
The driver asks if this is your first time in the city and recommends places to visit.
The card reader in the taxi is not working at first.

title: ホテルのチェックイン
role: a front desk agent at a large city hotel
setting: At the hotel front desk in the evening.
goal: Check in with your reservation, and ask about the checkout time and how to connect to the Wi-Fi.
goal_ja: 予約名を伝えてチェックインし、チェックアウトの時刻と Wi-Fi のつなぎ方を聞く
opener: Good evening! Are you checking in?
opener_ja: こんばんは！チェックインですか？

phrases.en: Yes, I have a reservation under Suzuki.
phrases.ja: はい、鈴木の名前で予約しています。

phrases.en: What time is checkout?
phrases.ja: チェックアウトは何時ですか？

phrases.en: How do I connect to the Wi-Fi?
phrases.ja: Wi-Fi はどうやってつなぎますか？

phrases.en: Could I get a late checkout?
phrases.ja: レイトチェックアウトはできますか？

twists: Your room is not ready yet and the agent asks you to wait or come back later.
The agent offers a room upgrade for an extra fee.
The agent asks for a credit card for incidentals.

title: カフェで注文する
role: a friendly barista at a busy coffee shop
setting: At the counter of a coffee shop in the morning.
goal: Order a drink with one change (size, milk, or ice), answer the barista's questions, and pay.
goal_ja: サイズやミルクなどを1つ指定して飲み物を注文し、質問に答えて支払う
opener: Hi! What can I get started for you?
opener_ja: こんにちは！ご注文は何にしますか？

phrases.en: Can I get a medium latte, please?
phrases.ja: ラテのMサイズをください。

phrases.en: Could I have it with oat milk?
phrases.ja: オーツミルクにできますか？

phrases.en: It's for here.
phrases.ja: 店内で飲みます。

phrases.en: That's all, thanks.
phrases.ja: 以上です。ありがとう。

twists: The oat milk is sold out today.
The barista mishears your name.
The barista recommends the seasonal special drink.

title: レストランで食事
role: a server at a casual American restaurant
setting: At a restaurant for dinner, sitting at a table.
goal: Ask for a recommendation, order a main dish and a drink, mention one food you can't eat, and ask for the check at the end.
goal_ja: おすすめを聞いて料理と飲み物を注文し、苦手な食べ物を1つ伝え、最後に会計を頼む
opener: Hi, I'm Jessica, and I'll be your server tonight. Can I start you off with something to drink?
opener_ja: こんばんは、今夜担当するジェシカです。まずお飲み物はいかがですか？

phrases.en: What do you recommend?
phrases.ja: おすすめは何ですか？

phrases.en: I'll have the chicken sandwich, please.
phrases.ja: チキンサンドをお願いします。

phrases.en: Could I get it without onions?
phrases.ja: 玉ねぎ抜きにできますか？

phrases.en: Could we get the check, please?
phrases.ja: お会計をお願いします。

twists: The dish you want is sold out tonight.
The server asks how you would like your steak or eggs cooked.
The check has an item you did not order.

title: 買い物をする
role: a sales associate at a clothing store
setting: In a clothing store at a shopping mall.
goal: Ask for a different size of a jacket, ask if you can try it on, and ask about the return policy before you buy it.
goal_ja: ジャケットの別のサイズを頼んで試着し、買う前に返品の条件を聞く
opener: Hi! Are you looking for anything in particular today?
opener_ja: こんにちは！今日は何かお探しですか？

phrases.en: Do you have this in a medium?
phrases.ja: これのMサイズはありますか？

phrases.en: Can I try it on?
phrases.ja: 試着してもいいですか？

phrases.en: What's your return policy?
phrases.ja: 返品の条件はどうなっていますか？

phrases.en: I'll take it.
phrases.ja: これにします。

twists: Your size is out of stock in this store, but available online.
There is a sale today: buy one, get one 50% off.
The fitting room line is long, so the associate suggests another option.

title: 街で道を聞く
role: a friendly local person walking on the street
setting: On a busy street downtown in the afternoon.
goal: Ask how to get to the nearest subway station, check how long it takes to walk, and repeat the directions back to confirm.
goal_ja: 最寄りの駅への行き方と歩く時間を聞き、道順を言い直して確かめる
opener: Hi, you look a little lost. Can I help you?
opener_ja: こんにちは、ちょっと迷っているみたいですね。お手伝いしましょうか？

phrases.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the subway station?
phrases.ja: すみません、地下鉄の駅にはどう行けばいいですか？

phrases.en: Is it within walking distance?
phrases.ja: 歩いて行ける距離ですか？

phrases.en: So I turn right at the second light?
phrases.ja: 2つ目の信号を右ですね？

phrases.en: Thank you so much.
phrases.ja: 本当にありがとうございます。

twists: The local person is also not sure and suggests asking at a nearby store.
The station is closed for repairs, so you need to take a bus instead.
The local person gives directions very quickly and you need to ask them to slow down.

title: 薬局で相談する
setting: At the pharmacy counter of a drugstore.
goal: Explain that you have a headache and a sore throat, ask what medicine you can buy, and check how often to take it.
goal_ja: 頭痛とのどの痛みを伝え、買える薬と飲み方（回数）を確かめる
opener: Hi, how can I help you today?
opener_ja: こんにちは。今日はどうされましたか？

phrases.en: I have a headache and a sore throat.
phrases.ja: 頭痛とのどの痛みがあります。

phrases.en: Do I need a prescription for this?
phrases.ja: これは処方箋が必要ですか？

phrases.en: How often should I take it?
phrases.ja: どのくらいの間隔で飲めばいいですか？

phrases.en: Does it make you sleepy?
phrases.ja: 眠くなりますか？

twists: The pharmacist asks if you are allergic to any medicine.
The medicine you ask for needs a prescription, so the pharmacist suggests another one.
The pharmacist recommends seeing a doctor if it does not get better in a few days.

title: 週末の予定を雑談
role: Emma, a friendly coworker from an overseas office who is visiting your team
setting: During a coffee break at the office on Friday afternoon.
goal: Make small talk about weekend plans: ask about Emma's plans, share yours, and recommend one place or food in your city.
goal_ja: 週末の予定を聞き合い、自分の予定を話して、地元のおすすめを1つ紹介する
opener: Happy Friday! Do you have any plans for the weekend?
opener_ja: やっと金曜日ですね！週末は何か予定がありますか？

phrases.en: Not much, I'm just going to relax at home.
phrases.ja: 特に何も。家でのんびりする予定です。

phrases.en: How about you?
phrases.ja: あなたは？

phrases.en: You should try the ramen place near the station.
phrases.ja: 駅の近くのラーメン屋に行ってみてください。

phrases.en: Have a great weekend!
phrases.ja: よい週末を！

twists: Emma invites you to join her weekend plan.
Emma asks about a Japanese custom and you need to explain it simply.
Emma's plans got canceled, so she asks you for ideas.
